content:
alex: Heads up: apac edge showing ~2% 503s for clients on IPv6 -> backend GPU services. Started ~2026-03-18T09:20:10Z
mina: seeing same metrics, latency spikes right before 503s, spike in egress NAT64 connections on lb-apac-2
sam: can you paste logs? sample curl from client?
alex: here's a curl from a repro device (over IPv6):
```
$ curl -v https://api.apac.redwood.test -H 'Host: gpu-svc'
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.apac.redwood.test/
*   Trying 2607:fb90:...:443...
* Connected to api.apac.redwood.test (2607:fb90:...) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake, then 503 Service Unavailable
```
irene: I think LB is answering AAAA but backend routing forces egress via our NAT64 translator pool, which translates to IPv4 egress nodes that are overloaded.
katie: that explains the weird capacity autoscaler behavior — autoscaler sees sudden TCP flows from NAT64 nodes and spins up more GPU instances for that path, cost spike + fragmenting load
mina: confirmed in lb logs: `client_ip_family=6 preserved=false nat64_proxy=pxy-eu-01` — we never set preserve-src on that LB variant
net-bot: healthcheck alert for lb-apac-2 at 09:22:14 UTC; backend pool `gpu-cluster-3` high syn backlog
sam: workaround: flip the apac LB to prefer A records for api.apac.redwood.test (force IPv4 client fallback) or enable `preserve-client-ip-v6: true` on lb-apac-2. Prefer preserve-src but that needs config rollout
irene: preserve-src rollout requires kernel patch on edge nodes (conntrack tweak). Might take 2hrs to stage
alex: quick mitigation — disable AAAA for the api subdomain in DNS for apac region only? impact on true IPv6-only clients = will force NAT64 at client side, safer? hmm
mina: disabling AAAA at DNS would force v4 for *resolving hosts* — IPv6-only clients relying on DNS64/NAT64 might break. We need to check client mix. Current errors are from dual-stack devices that prefer v6
katie: cost/ops decision: quick DNS change + ops note to remove after proper preserve-src rollout. Can we do a partial traffic steering? SRV/A weighting? not supported by mobile SDKs
sam: propose: 1) enable `preserve-client-ip-v6` on a canary LB (lb-apac-canary) 2) divert 10% traffic with a routing rule 3) monitor nat64 connection counts and 503s for 2h
alex: +1 for canary. If canary works, roll to lb-apac-2 and rollback DNS change. If not, keep DNS change and open follow-up for kernel conntrack fix
irene: I'll open the canary config PR and schedule the kernel patch job. ETA ~3 hours for PR -> canary deploy
mina: adding dashboards and alert tweaks: nat64_conn_count, client_ipv6_preserve rate, backend_syn_backlog
katie: creating a billing tag to track extra egress NAT64 cost over the incident window :money_with_wings:
alex: thanks. I'll coordinate with support to message customers if we do DNS flip. tagging @support on plan
support: noted — will prep customer comms if we flip DNS or see client impact
mina: final note: root cause likely LB variant defaulting to v6 rewrite on dualstack listeners. Need doc update on lb behavior + add e2e test for preserve-src
alex: ok — let's follow the canary plan. I'll update this thread with timestamps and roll progress :thumbsup:
